docs.title: About this research
docs.text:
Hafiyyan Hilmy Fawwaz · Urban Transportation and Planning Lab, Hiroshima University

A GPS staypoint rarely tells you which place a person actually visited: positional error is often larger than the gap between a building, the street in front of it and the open space beside it. This research builds a probabilistic framework that assigns each staypoint to an urban spatial entity (building, street or open space) under explicit positional uncertainty, instead of snapping it to the nearest one.

Dates are written DD-MM-YYYY.

docs.title: Alpha calibration
docs.text:
Analysis 21-07-2026

\(\alpha\) sets the width of f_distance's decay. It is calibrated by profile likelihood on Model 4a: for each α the other weights are refit, and LL(b) scores that α. Since \(f_\text{distance}(\alpha) = f_\text{distance}(1)^{1/\alpha^2}\), no rescoring is needed during the search.

α LL(b) Accuracy 1.0 -0.6881 0.717 2.0 -0.6708 0.726 2.4 -0.6701 0.723 3.0 -0.6707 0.720 4.0 -0.6725 0.720

Single peak; optimizer gives α* = 2.4297. Real rescoring at that value matches the shortcut to 2e-16.

  • Model 2's own optimum (2.106) transfers to 4a at almost no cost, and vice versa: the models agree on the decay width.
  • Calibrate once on 4a and re-derive downstream models, rather than recalibrating inside richer ones: for Models 5 and 6 that marginally raised LL, lowered accuracy and roughly doubled VIFs.
  • Model 1's surface is not single-peaked and no α fixes its core problem (Model 1: base).

Main payoff: The f_distance² artifact. On raw-density data the optimum moves: Raw-density alpha profile. Part of Chapter 5: Results.

docs.title: Candidate density bias toward building
docs.text:
Analysis 23-07-2026

It is not candidate sparsity. True street stays have the densest same-type pool:

True type Same-type candidates, mean median Total candidates, mean Building 7.09 5 22.99 Street 13.17 11 36.61 Open space 5.42 3 18.34

share_type penalizes a candidate for many same-type neighbours (share_street -8.09 in the Final model). Streets are drawn as many short adjacent GIS segments (Spatial entity layers), so a true street stay is penalized for density its own geometry creates. Probability then drifts to the nearest building (Confusion matrix).

This is a fixable artifact of the street layer, not a GPS-evidence ceiling (Contributions), but it undercuts the street-space motivation: Tension with the street-space argument, Candidate density as boundary-matching difficulty.

Part of Chapter 5: Results.

docs.title: Downsampling shrinks the candidate search area
docs.text:
Analysis 29-07-2026

At the same R_buffer = 10 m, raw-density scoring produced 36,110 candidate rows vs 22,484 downsampled: 1.6× more for the same 907 stays.

Not a bug: Candidate selection buffers the union of a stay's points, and about 9.9× more points cover more ground even though the radius is unchanged. Downsampling reduces the effective search area, not just the point count. Worth remembering if R_buffer sensitivity is revisited (R_buffer: 10 m vs 15 m).

Part of Raw-density refit.

docs.title: Confusion matrix
docs.text:
Analysis 23-07-2026

Final model, out-of-sample: each stay's prediction comes from the grouped-CV fold where it was held out.

actual predicted building street open space recall building 476 22 33 89.6% street 86 79 20 42.7% open space 86 11 94 49.2%
  • Building recall is about double the other two.
  • Both street and open space are misclassified as building (46.5%, 45.0%) far more than as each other (10.8%, 5.8%).
  • More street stays go to building (86) than are classified as street (79).

The in-sample matrix is nearly identical (building 89.8%, street 44.3%, open space 49.7%), so this is not an overfitting effect.

Analysis 21-07-2026

Does f_directional only mean something for streets? Both variants have 7 parameters, so they compare directly (not nested).

R=10 m 3a: shared 3b: street only LL(b) -0.7510 -0.7520 Accuracy 0.668 0.666 Building / street / open space 0.872 / 0.362 / 0.398 0.872 / 0.335 / 0.414 CV accuracy (grouped) 0.664 ± 0.046 0.658 ± 0.040 Condition number 117 135

docs.title: f_directional: shared vs split
docs.text:
Analysis 21-07-2026

Does f_directional need one coefficient per type ("split", the 14-parameter model) or one for all types ("shared", 12 parameters)? Everything else held fixed.

Shared (12) Split (14) Street only (12) Accuracy 0.721 0.724 0.723 CV accuracy (grouped) 0.716 ± 0.076 0.709 ± 0.075 0.716 ± 0.069 Condition number 1,373 2,430 1,431

Split vs shared: LR = 5.41, df = 2, p = 0.067, not significant. The split's two extra parameters buy +0.3 pp in-sample but lower CV and double the condition number: it overfits (Overfitting signature).

The shared coefficient is cleanly significant (t = +3.12); in the split version only the building term clears 1.96. Street-only is statistically equivalent to shared at this size, never better; at the 7-parameter size shared wins on every metric (CV 0.666 vs 0.656), echoing Directional scope ablation (3a vs 3b).

Decision: shared, 12 parameters → Final model, adopted as the thesis's final model (Section 5.1.8). Part of Chapter 5: Results.

Linked from Chapter 5: Results · Directional scope ablation (3a vs 3b) · Overfitting signature · RQ1 rebuilt with grouped CV · Stepwise VIF elimination · f_directional

docs.title: The f_distance² artifact
docs.text:
Analysis 21-07-2026

At α = 1, a squared distance term was clearly significant (t = 3.81) in the Interaction term screen (α = 1). After Alpha calibration (α = 2.4297), the same screen re-run from scratch gives t = 0.50.

The squared term was compensating for a too-narrow decay, not capturing real nonlinearity. It also caused most of Model 6's conditioning problem.

Screen term t at α = 1 t at α = 2.4297 f_distance² 3.81 0.50 σ² 2.23 2.47 f_distribution × σ -0.15 0.32 f_distance × f_directional 0.11 1.73 f_distribution × share_type 5.58 4.91

Lesson: re-derive the term selection at the calibrated α; bolting the new α onto old terms doubled VIFs instead (condition number 20,695 → 48,275).

One case of Overfitting signature. Next: Model 6, re-derived at calibrated alpha. Part of Chapter 5: Results.

Sensei asked whether Random Forest or XGBoost would show the ceiling once nonlinearity is free. Both were fit as 3-class classifiers on the logit's 13 raw ingredients, one row per stay, no hand-built interactions, with stay-level CV.

docs.text:
Analysis 23-07-2026

Random Forest and XGBoost on the same row-level task as the logit (one row per stay-candidate pair), raw unsplit features plus a one-hot type, on the identical grouped-CV folds.

docs.text:
Analysis 21-07-2026

Drops f_temporal, adds share_type per type and one sigma term:

\[V_k = w_1 f_\text{distribution} + w_2 f_\text{distance} + w_3 f_\text{directional} + w_4\,share_\text{bldg} + w_5\,share_\text{street} + w_6\,share_\text{os} + w_7\,\sigma\] R=10 m R=15 m ρ² vs LL(C) 0.198 0.199 Accuracy 0.668 0.654 Building / street / open space 0.872 / 0.362 / 0.398 0.881 / 0.308 / 0.356 CV accuracy (grouped) 0.664 ± 0.046 0.647 ± 0.042 Condition number 117 98 Term (R=10 m) w t f_distribution +3.542 8.40 f_distance -1.209 -2.60 f_directional +1.708 5.89 share_bldg +0.219 0.76 share_street -5.552 -15.68 share_os -5.887 -12.79 sigma +0.475 5.87
  • Now beats the type-share baseline; accuracy +15 pp over Model 1: base.
  • The gain is a building story: building jumps from ~0.58 to ~0.87, street is flat to worse, open space worse. share_street/share_os dominate and pull probability toward buildings, an early sign of Candidate density bias toward building.
  • sigma is a clean positive effect; f_directional becomes significant once f_temporal is gone.
  • f_distance now flips sign significantly between radii.

docs.title: Model 4a: alternative-specific parameters
docs.text:
Analysis 21-07-2026

Every score gets its own weight per type; sigma stays shared. 13 parameters:

\[V_t = w_{1,t} f_\text{distribution} + w_{2,t} f_\text{distance} + w_{3,t} f_\text{directional} + w_{4,t}\,share_t + w_5\,\sigma\] Model 4a (R=10 m, α=1) ρ² vs LL(C) 0.265 LR vs 3a (df=6) 114.15, p < 1e-16 Accuracy 0.717 Building / street / open space 0.902 / 0.443 / 0.466 CV accuracy (grouped) 0.707 ± 0.069 Condition number 775

All three types improve at once for the first time (building +3 pp, street +8.1 pp, open space +6.8 pp). Max VIF 10.69 on f_directional_street; the high within-type correlations are Multicollinearity is structural.

f_distance_bldg and f_distance_street are not individually significant (t = 0.29, 0.34): part of the distance signal is absorbed by share and sigma once split by type.

Becomes the base for everything after. Next: Model 5: alternative-specific constants (rejected), Interaction term screen (α = 1). Alpha is calibrated on this model: Alpha calibration. Part of Chapter 5: Results.

docs.title: Model 5: alternative-specific constants (rejected)
docs.text:
Analysis 21-07-2026

Model 4a: alternative-specific parameters plus asc_street, asc_os (building = reference), 15 parameters.

4a 5 (+ ASC) Accuracy 0.717 0.728 CV accuracy (grouped) 0.707 ± 0.069 0.717 ± 0.068 LR vs 4a (df=2) 29.6, p < 0.0001 Max VIF 10.69 39.76 Condition number 775 37,583

Formally significant, but the CV gain is within one standard deviation, and asc_street ↔ f_directional_street r = 0.96: f_directional is nearly constant within street candidates, so the model is asked to estimate the same "street-ness" twice. The directional terms and asc_street get standard errors around 4.5 and lose significance; CV estimates swing by 60-65% of their mean.

At 15 m it gets worse (condition number 92,891) and some CV folds diverge to coefficients in the thousands. Calibrating alpha adds two more near-duplicate pairs (asc_t ↔ f_distance_t, r = 0.98).

Rejected on reliability grounds. One case of Overfitting signature. Part of Chapter 5: Results.

Analysis 23-07-2026

sigma has a modest logit coefficient (+0.78 in the Final model) yet tree models rank it at or near the top:

Run σ rank Stay-level, RF impurity / XGBoost gain 2nd / 2nd Stay-level, out-of-fold permutation RF 1st, XGBoost 2nd Row-level, RF impurity 1st (0.31) Row-level, XGBoost gain 2nd, after the building indicator

Analysis 21-07-2026

docs.title: Candidate density as boundary-matching difficulty
docs.text:
Note 23-07-2026

A narrower analogue exists in the positional-error literature. Weng et al. (2025) need sidewalk matching because sidewalks are about 2 m wide while raw urban-canyon error reaches 18.4 m RMS static and up to 32 m cross-street dynamic. Quddus et al. (2007) note that point-to-curve matching is unstable at high road density, belief-theory matching degrades on parallel streets, and Y-junctions are ambiguous when both links are almost equally close.

Candidate density bias toward building is a similar problem one level up: densely packed same-type candidates give small noise more chances to land on the wrong one.

The limit of the analogy: those papers resolve between alternatives of the same kind, while the street disadvantage here is a between-type competition (street losing to building). The shared root is closely packed candidates, not an identical mechanism.

Part of Chapter 6: Discussion and conclusion (a subsection of the thesis's Discussion).

Linked from Candidate density bias toward building · Chapter 2: Literature · Chapter 6: Discussion and conclusion · Discussion citation checks

docs.text:
Note 25-07-2026

A stay's candidates are the entities that intersect the union of its GPS points, each buffered by R_buffer. The same radius is used inside f_distribution, on purpose.

R_buffer = 10 m was chosen over 15 m: R_buffer: 10 m vs 15 m. Because the search area is a union of buffered points, more points mean a larger area: Downsampling shrinks the candidate search area.

docs.title: Experiment design
docs.text:
Note 25-07-2026

The ground truth comes from a controlled field survey:

docs.title: f_directional
docs.text:
Note 25-07-2026

Bearing alignment with the street's orientation. For buildings and open spaces it is computed as 1 − max alignment with any adjacent street, so it carries a value for every candidate.

How to specify it took three tests: Directional scope ablation (3a vs 3b), its collinearity with an ASC in Model 5: alternative-specific constants (rejected), and finally f_directional: shared vs split, which settled on one coefficient shared across types.

docs.title: f_distance
docs.text:
Note 25-07-2026

Gaussian decay with distance, its width scaled by the cluster's dispersion \(\sigma_i\) and a calibrated factor \(\alpha\):

\[f_{\text{distance}}(E_k, C_i) = \exp\left(-\frac{d_{ki}^2}{2(\alpha \cdot \sigma_i)^2}\right)\]

\(\alpha\) was 1.0 (uncalibrated) until Alpha calibration set it to 2.4297. Before that, its coefficient flipped sign between radii (Model 1: base, Model 2: share-type and sigma) and a squared term appeared significant for the wrong reason (The f_distance² artifact).

Part of Framework overview.

docs.text:

docs.text:

docs.title: Framework overview
docs.text:
Note 25-07-2026

  1. Candidates: every entity within R_buffer of the stay cluster (Candidate selection).
  2. Scores: four components per candidate: f_distribution, f_distance, f_temporal, f_directional.
  3. Utility: a weighted sum \(V_k\) of the scores (plus share_type and sigma once calibration added them).
  4. Probability: a type-level conditional logit,
\[P(t \mid C_i) = \frac{\sum_{k \in t} \exp(V_k)}{\sum_j \exp(V_j)}\]

The weights are estimated by maximum likelihood on the Ground truth dataset rather than fixed in advance.

Part of Chapter 4: Framework. Answers the "how" of Research questions RQ1.

docs.title: Grouped cross-validation
docs.text:
Note 21-07-2026

Each physical stop was recorded by up to 3 devices at once (Experiment design), so up to 3 stay records share one label and context. Plain stratified CV can put siblings in both train and test, which leaks and inflates accuracy.

Since 21-07-2026 every CV number uses StratifiedGroupKFold (5 folds) grouped by physical stop (participant and stop sequence), so siblings always share a fold. The whole progression was refit under it (Model progression).

Effect on the headline: in-sample accuracy unchanged (~0.724), but CV became 0.709 ± 0.075 for the 14-parameter model instead of the earlier 0.716 ± 0.035. The wider band is the honest one. Earlier stay-level CV results, such as ML baseline, stay level (superseded), are superseded.

docs.title: Extending map matching to stationary stays
docs.text:
Note 23-07-2026

Bierlaire et al. (2013), Chen and Bierlaire (2015) and Kempinska et al. (2016) all generate probabilities from a chain: dependency between adjacent GPS points, a first-order Markov structure, or a particle filter stepping through time. A single stationary cluster has no upstream point, previous timestep or adjacent segment.

What carries over is the commitment to several plausible entities with likelihoods. What does not is the mechanism: this framework scores properties intrinsic to one static cluster (Framework overview). Quddus et al. (2007) support that this substitution is necessary: fix-by-fix matching without trajectory history risks selecting the wrong link, and off-network cases such as car parks are named as an unresolved limitation.

Part of Chapter 6: Discussion and conclusion (a subsection of the thesis's Discussion). Motivated in Motivation.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text:
Note 25-07-2026

Deterministic GPS-to-entity assignment (nearest or containing building) has two structural problems:

  1. It leaves out streets and open spaces as activity locations, although urban theory (Jacobs, Gehl, Whyte) treats them as real sites of activity (Tension with the street-space argument).
  2. It ignores positional uncertainty by forcing a single match.

Probabilistic assignment exists for moving segments (map matching), but its logic had not been extended to stationary stay clusters, nor combined with a multi-target building/street/open-space scope (Extending map matching to stationary stays).

Part of Chapter 1: Introduction. Leads to Research questions.

Linked from Chapter 1: Introduction · Extending map matching to stationary stays · Thesis summary

docs.title: Multicollinearity is structural
docs.text:
Note 19-07-2026

In alternative-specific models, each type's own features (f_distance_t, f_directional_t, share_t) come from the same per-stay candidate pool, so they correlate strongly within a type (often r = 0.86-0.94), and VIFs above 10 appear on core terms.

This is a property of the design, not redundant feature choice. Getting every VIF under 10 would mean removing components from the alternative-specific structure, which would undo why it beats the generic models (Model 4a: alternative-specific parameters). The elimination procedure therefore protects the core terms (Stepwise VIF elimination).

What is not structural: an ASC that duplicates a near-constant feature (Model 5: alternative-specific constants (rejected)).

Seen in Final model correlation matrix. Part of Chapter 5: Results.

Linked from Chapter 5: Results · Final model correlation matrix · MNL model development · Model 4a: alternative-specific parameters · Stepwise VIF elimination

docs.title: Overfitting signature
docs.text:
Note 25-07-2026

Across the calibration, extra complexity repeatedly bought in-sample gains without matching CV gains:

  1. Adding an ASC: Model 5: alternative-specific constants (rejected)
  2. Splitting f_directional by type: f_directional: shared vs split
  3. The squared distance term at uncalibrated alpha: The f_distance² artifact

Tree models show it at larger scale: both beat the logit in-sample and lose to it under grouped CV (ML ceiling check, row level).

Why it matters for MILES: the ground truth's 59/20/21 type split is a design artifact (Ground truth dataset), and share_type weights fit sample-specific patterns, so transfer to MILES's unknown type mix is an untested risk (Limitations).

Answers Research questions RQ3. Part of Chapter 5: Results.

docs.title: Positioning against deterministic assignment
docs.text:
Note 23-07-2026

Two deterministic mechanisms from Chapter 2: SMoT tests whether a trajectory segment stays inside a candidate-stop polygon for a minimum time (Alvares et al., 2007), and Wu et al. (2026) assign each GPS point to its nearest entity. Both commit to one entity and carry no confidence.

Wu et al. do define a misclassification probability that depends on GPS error and on closeness to an entity's boundary, but only as an after-the-fact accuracy bound. This framework builds that boundary-and-error logic into the assignment and returns a distribution, at grouped CV accuracy 0.716 ± 0.076 (Final model).

Would a more flexible model do better? RQ3 says no: Random Forest and XGBoost fit closer in-sample (0.762, 0.849 vs 0.721) but generalize worse (0.699, 0.695 vs 0.716) (ML ceiling check, row level). The advantage is complexity matched to what generalizes, while staying interpretable as twelve signed coefficients.

Part of Chapter 6: Discussion and conclusion (a subsection of the thesis's Discussion). Literature: Chapter 2: Literature.

Linked from Chapter 2: Literature · Chapter 6: Discussion and conclusion · Discussion citation checks

docs.title: Research questions
docs.text:
Note 25-07-2026

Objective: a probabilistic assignment framework that gives GPS stay clusters probabilities over buildings, streets and open spaces, with positional uncertainty built in through cluster-derived spatial and temporal metrics.

  • RQ1: How can positional uncertainty be incorporated into a probabilistic, multi-target assignment framework? → Framework overview, calibration in Chapter 5: Results
  • RQ2: To what extent does the framework's output agree with ground truth? → Confusion matrix

Note 19-07-2026

How common the candidate's own type is among the stay's candidates, given a separate coefficient per type (share_bldg, share_street, share_os).

docs.title: sigma
docs.text:
Note 19-07-2026

Stay-level positional dispersion, \(\sigma = \sqrt{\mathrm{var}(x) + \mathrm{var}(y)}\), standardized once by sigma_scale = 36.708 (99th-percentile cap 179.14 m) and reused unchanged in every model.

It enters with one shared coefficient and building as the reference (0 for building rows). Splitting it by type is an identification problem, not a modelling option.

Clean positive effect in every model (Model 2: share-type and sigma, Final model), yet tree models rank it far higher than its modest coefficient suggests: Sigma in tree importance.

docs.text:
Note 25-07-2026

Three entity types, mutually exclusive by construction:

Type Source Building ZTOWN footprints, unmodified Street MAPPLE centerlines, buffered by street width Open space The residual area after erasing streets and buildings from the street-network extent

Streets are drawn as many short adjacent segments, which matters later: Candidate density bias toward building. Underground arcades are not in ZTOWN, which is why some stays had to be dropped: Ground truth drop list.

docs.title: Tension with the street-space argument
docs.text:
Note 23-07-2026

The framework gives streets and open spaces equal standing because Jacobs, Gehl and Whyte treat them as real sites of activity. RQ2 complicates that: building recall 89.6% vs street 42.7% and open space 49.2%, with both losing mostly to building (Confusion matrix).

The cause is a calibration artifact, not weaker GPS evidence: share_type penalizes candidates with many same-type neighbours, and street candidates are about 1.9× denser than buildings' (mean 13.17 vs 7.09) because streets are drawn as many short segments (Candidate density bias toward building).

Two readings stay open: an artifact of this street layer (fewer, longer segments would narrow it), or a general disadvantage of elongated, repeated entity types under any density-based mechanism. No reviewed source settles it (Discussion citation checks); testing other segmentation schemes would (Future work).

Part of Chapter 6: Discussion and conclusion (a subsection of the thesis's Discussion).

docs.text:
Progress 19-07-2026

First calibration on the cleaned 907-stay ground truth.

  • R_buffer = 10 m beats 15 m for every model: R_buffer: 10 m vs 15 m.
  • Six specifications compared: Model 1: base → Model 2: share-type and sigma → Directional scope ablation (3a vs 3b) → Model 4a: alternative-specific parameters → Model 5: alternative-specific constants (rejected) → Interaction term screen (α = 1). Accuracy rose from 0.518 to about 0.724.
  • α calibrated to about 2.4 on Model 4a (Alpha calibration); re-deriving the interaction terms at that α dropped f_distance² (The f_distance² artifact).
  • Leading model at the time: alternative-specific terms + f_distribution × share_type, 14 parameters, accuracy 0.724.
  • High VIFs on core terms are a property of the design: Multicollinearity is structural.

Later corrected by RQ1 rebuilt with grouped CV.

docs.text:
Progress 21-07-2026

  • Earlier CV leaked sibling-device recordings across folds; every model was refit with Grouped cross-validation (Model progression).
  • Same model shape, same in-sample accuracy (0.724), but CV is 0.709 ± 0.075, a wider and more honest band.
  • Alpha calibration reproduced α* = 2.4297; Model 5: alternative-specific constants (rejected) and The f_distance² artifact reconfirmed; Stepwise VIF elimination gave the 14-parameter model.

docs.title: Thesis summary
docs.text:
Progress 13-10-2026

Beyond the Building: A Probabilistic Framework for GPS Assignment Under Positional Uncertainty

A GPS stay cluster rarely tells us which place a person visited: positional error is often larger than the gap between a building, the street in front of it and the open space beside it. This thesis assigns each stay cluster a probability over buildings, streets and open spaces instead of snapping it to the nearest entity, and calibrates that assignment against a controlled field-survey ground truth.
